slides: Here are two more circle tools. They come up in some of the harder circle questions. And right after this lesson, two questions teach two more tools.

slides.say: First, let's look at two equal circles, where each one passes through the center of the other. Here's a circle with center O, and an equal circle with center P. P is on the first circle, and O is on the second one.
at: Here's a circle with center O

slides.say: The circles cross at two points, A and B. What can we say about this shape? No angle is given, so we add helper lines. We join the centers to the crossing points.
at: The circles cross at two points

slides.say: O A and O B are radii of the first circle. P A and P B are radii of the second circle. And O P? P is on the first circle, so O P is also a radius. The circles are equal, so all five segments have the same length, r.
at: so O P is also a radius

slides.say: So triangle O A P has three equal sides. It's equilateral, and triangle O B P is equilateral too. Every angle in them is sixty degrees.

Now the angle A O B. It's made of the two angles at O, one from each equilateral triangle. It's sixty plus sixty, a hundred twenty degrees. And a hundred twenty degrees is a third of the circle, because three times a hundred twenty is three hundred sixty.
This needs both conditions, equal circles, and each center on the other circle. Equal circles that are farther apart give a different angle, like the ninety degrees in the union question.
Questions love the region the two circles share, the shape in the middle. Draw the chord A B. It cuts this shape into two equal pieces.

Look at the right piece. It's between the chord A B and an arc of the circle with center O. Take the sector A O B, a third of that circle. Then take away triangle A O B. What's left is exactly the right piece.
The left piece is the same, in the circle with center P. So the shared region is two times, the sector minus the triangle.
Let's see it in numbers. Say the radius is six. The whole circle is pi times six squared, thirty-six pi. The sector A O B is a third of it. Thirty-six pi divided by three is twelve pi.

Now triangle A O B. The four radii make a rhombus, O A P B. Let's take it out. O P cuts it into our two equilateral triangles. Remember, the area of every equilateral triangle is a squared, times root three, over four. Here a is six. Six squared is thirty-six, and thirty-six over four is nine. So each one is nine root three.

So each one is nine root three

slides.say: Now cut the same rhombus the other way, with the chord A B. A diagonal cuts a rhombus into two equal halves, and triangle A O B is one of them. So it's half of the rhombus, the same as one equilateral triangle, nine root three.
So one piece is twelve pi minus nine root three. The shared region is two pieces, so we double the whole difference.

slides.say: Two times twelve pi is twenty-four pi. And two times nine root three is eighteen root three. So the shared region is twenty-four pi minus eighteen root three.

Let's try one more, with a radius of two. The circle is four pi, so the sector is a third of it, four pi over three. Each equilateral triangle is two squared, times root three, over four. Four over four is one, so it's root three.

slides.say: So the shared region is two times, four pi over three minus root three. That's eight pi over three, minus two root three.

slides.say: The second tool is a ring. Two circles with the same center, O, and the ring between them. Circles with the same center are called concentric. Call the big radius big R, and the small radius r. The ring is the big circle minus the small circle, pi big R squared minus pi r squared.
at: Two circles with the same center
The ring is the big circle

slides.say: Now a chord A B of the big circle that just touches the small circle, at the point M. M is a point of tangency, so the automatic helper line is the radius O M. It's perpendicular to the chord.

Draw O A and O B too. They're radii of the big circle, so triangle A O B is isosceles. O M is the height to its base, and in an isosceles triangle that height is also a median. So M cuts the chord in half. Call each half h.
at: Draw O A and O B
So M cuts the chord in half

slides.say: Look at the right triangle O M B. Its legs are r and h, and its hypotenuse is big R. By Pythagoras, r squared plus h squared is big R squared. Now subtract r squared from both sides. So big R squared minus r squared is h squared.
at: Now subtract r squared from both sides

slides.say: And the ring? Let's go back to the whole ring. Pi big R squared minus pi r squared is pi times, big R squared minus r squared. That's pi times h squared. So the ring depends only on the chord.

The ring is the big circle minus the small one. A hundred sixty-nine pi minus a hundred forty-four pi is twenty-five pi, just like the rule says.
Radii five and five root two, a silver triangle with legs five and five. Five root two, squared, is fifty. Fifty pi minus twenty-five pi is twenty-five pi again.
